terminal.help.title: Terminal
terminal.help.intro: Terminal is a real server console inside the browser. Each tab is backed by tmux, so you can leave and come back without stopping what was left running.
terminal.help.first.title: First steps
terminal.help.first.step1: Open “New session” and choose Claude TUI or Terminal.
terminal.help.first.step2: Choose the project or folder where you want to work.
terminal.help.first.step3: Type commands as in any terminal; in Claude TUI, type your requests for the assistant.
terminal.help.first.step4: Switch tabs by tapping a Sessions card or a chip in the narrow rail.
terminal.help.first.step5: On mobile, expand the ⌨ bar to use Esc, Tab, Ctrl, arrows, paste, or dictation.
terminal.help.legend.title: Legend
terminal.help.legend.terminal.name: Terminal with Claude
terminal.help.legend.terminal.desc: the rail detected a Claude model inside the session
terminal.help.legend.shell.name: Shell
terminal.help.legend.shell.desc: regular terminal with no Claude detected
terminal.help.legend.chat.name: Chat
terminal.help.legend.chat.desc: visual conversation; it can switch to TUI without changing sessions
terminal.help.legend.working.name: Working
terminal.help.legend.working.desc: animated dot: the session is producing activity
terminal.help.legend.waiting.name: Waiting
terminal.help.legend.waiting.desc: green dot: the session is waiting for your input
terminal.help.legend.idle.name: Idle
terminal.help.legend.idle.desc: dim dot: no active work was detected
terminal.help.legend.close.name: Close tab
terminal.help.legend.close.desc: removes the browser view but does not kill the tmux session
terminal.help.actions.title: Buttons and actions
terminal.help.actions.input.v: Everything you type is sent to the real server process. A request to Claude TUI consumes tokens.
terminal.help.actions.link.v: Links recognized in the output can be tapped or clicked.
terminal.help.actions.paste.v: Attempts to paste clipboard text into the terminal.
terminal.help.actions.scroll.v: Scrolls through history; if the application captures the mouse, it sends wheel events to that program.
terminal.help.actions.card.v: Opens the terminal or focuses its tab if it is already visible.
terminal.help.actions.chip.v: Switches tabs when the right sidebar is collapsed on desktop.
terminal.help.actions.close.v: Closes only the local tab. The session stays alive so it can be resumed from Sessions.
terminal.help.actions.aux.v: Expands Esc, Tab, ⇧Tab, Ctrl, arrows, ^C, /, paste, and dictation for a Terminal or TUI.
terminal.help.compare.title: When to use each one
terminal.help.compare.chat.v: Best for conversation, reviewing tools and permissions, attaching files, and reading formatted history.
terminal.help.compare.tui.v: Best when you need the full Claude Code interface, its slash commands, or an interactive terminal flow. It consumes tokens when responding to requests.
terminal.help.compare.shell.v: Best for shell, logs, and interactive programs. It does not use AI unless you start one yourself.
terminal.help.persistence.title: Why it survives
terminal.help.persistence.text: The tab is only a window into a tmux session that lives on the server. Closing the browser closes that window, not the process; if the web console restarts, it detects its own sessions again and reattaches.
terminal.help.warning.title: Watch out for this
terminal.help.warning.text: “Kill session” from the ⋯ menu ends tmux and everything running inside it. Claude TUI starts without asking for permissions, and a Terminal runs commands exactly as you type them. Persistence covers closing the browser or restarting the web console, not rebooting the machine.
